remediation_detail: Two-model review. Stage-1 Opus: S9-1(sev-8 BLOCKER) engine mounted flag-independently (ran a 2nd receive engine + concurrent group.ingest race + durable writes for all users flag-OFF) -> mount gated on isEngineReadPathEnabled()&&readyForEngine; S9-2(sev-4) flag-OFF-doesn't-run regression test. Stage-2 Fable: F1(sev-6 doc) flag-ON dual-ingest caveat + recorded S12 prerequisite (retire device-sync group.ingest driver); F2(sev-2) deepened convergence to full-Task deep-equality; F3(sev-2) loading=Set{uninitialized,joining,catching_up}. Both models converge-verified clean. Verification: 6/7 questions YES; VQ-S9-003 (deletability) NO adjudicated by base:decider -> ACCEPT: pre-existing task-store cross-module coupling (marmot/client, device-sync, device-store, mls-trace) NOT introduced by S9 (all S9 NEW imports within dependencies_allowed); full task-store seam-isolation is epic-level debt owned by S12/S13 (re-raise VQ-S9-003 against them if not driven to zero). AC-MIG-2 amended (role-based strangler-toggle carve-out, both models concurred).
decider_caveats: VQ-S9-003 deletability NO ACCEPTED as pre-existing coupling (not an S9 regression); full task-store seam-isolation deferred to S12/S13.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: Two compounding gaps made this story materially harder than 'add a flag and delegate reads': (1) AC-MIG-2's own text ('no new if/switch/ternary branches') is, taken literally, impossible to satisfy for a GENUINE runtime toggle -- selecting between two data sources requires at least one conditional construct in any language. The story brief anticipated this ('the single feature-flag branch you add must be offset... OR structured so it is not net-new branching') but the diff check still nets +1 (1 added ConditionalExpression, 0 removable/relocatable branches existed in task-store.tsx, which was diff-identical to the da36c2b baseline before this story). Resolved by making it the ONLY conditional in the file, feeding a single downstream consumer, and reporting the exact number rather than gaming the grep with array-indexing or other keyword-dodging tricks. (2) Wiring 'the real marmot-adapter via a factory' into a genuinely-functioning engine required a full PersistenceAdapter, but S4's raw-event-log-store.ts only implements 4 of 10 methods -- the other 6 (checkpoint/deferred) are S11's explicit, not-yet-landed deliverable, sequenced AFTER S9 in the epic's own dependency order. Neither gap is discoverable by reading S9's story text alone; both required tracing stories.json's dependency_notes, spec.md's Phase ordering, and receive-engine.ts's actual start()/loadCheckpoint call graph to confirm.
retrospective.surprised_by: react-engine-hooks.ts's useReceiveEngine returns a freshly-constructed {projection, engineState, lastRejection} object literal on every render (not memoized). Wiring a naive forwarding useEffect keyed on that whole object (rather than its individual fields) in EngineTaskBridge created an actual infinite render loop that OOM-killed the vitest worker process (heap exhaustion, not a clean assertion failure) -- caught only because the test suite crashed rather than hung silently. Recorded as VQ-S9-010 and captured as a durable learning (base:learnings) so a future consumer of this hook doesn't rediscover it the same way.
